newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-HEYNCKES PLANNING TO BUILD ON REAL'S STRENGTHS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HEYNCKES PLANNING TO BUILD ON REAL'S STRENGTHS.

text.p: Real Madrid's new coach Jupp Heynckes, who has a reputation for being controversial and authoritarian, plans no sweeping changes to the Spanish champions in the short term.

Speaking to the media on Wednesday for the first time since he signed a two-year contract, the 52-year-old German said former coach Fabio Capello had put together an impressive outfit before returning to AC Milan.
"Last season Fabio Capello formed a new team and was very successful with it," the former international striker said.
"I'm not going to put together a new team without any reason. I like the present team a lot and last season I was very impressed by them. They are very professional and very disciplined."
Heynckes, who has been given a contract worth 200 million pesatas a year ($1.37 millon), can be a charming man in private but he believes in getting his way when it comes to running the team.
His sometimes turbulent periods in charge of German clubs Bayern Munich and Eintracht Frankfurt provide evidence for that.

Now Heynckes, who can be prone to say the wrong thing in public, has the job of improving the morale of the Real players who have performed poorly in the last seven weeks despite securing their 15th Spanish title.
Real Madrid's campaign, which saw them win the title by two points from rivals Barcelona, finished on Sunday in dismal fashion with a 4-0 defeat at Celta.
"There are many things to consider in the coming months but maybe I'll give them a bit more freedom to move around the pitch," he said.
"I hope to become a part of Spanish Cup history. I'm very happy to be at this club. It is an exceptional club."
Last season Heynckes guided Tenerife to ninth place in the league. The club from the Canary Islands also reached the semifinals of the UEFA Cup.
However he had become increasingly dissatisfied with the lack of resources at his disposal.
Heynckes had been the media favourite for the coach's job with the Spanish champions ever since Capello announced on April 28 that he was going to leave Real at the end of the season.
One man who can feel a bit more confident about his future at Real Madrid is Germany's former World Cup-winning goalkeeper Bodo Illgner.
Illgner had been critcised by Capello and the other players for not joining in the club's social activities.
But Heynckes said emphatically: "Bodo is my keeper."

The new Real Madrid coach also denied speculation that he was going to bring in new, young players from Germany like he had done at Tenerife and during his reign as coach at another Spanish club, Athletic Bilbao.
High on the list of priorities is a good showing in the European Cup. Despite having won the competition six times, Real Madrid's last triumph was in 1966.
Satisfying the fanatical Real fans will not be easy, however.
In a recent poll conducted by a Spanish newspaper, Heynckes finished a poor third behind Borussia Dortmund's former coach Ottmar Hitzfeld as the fans' favourite candidate for the job.
